Kazanow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kazanów, Poland

Demolished. Jews are first recorded in Kazanów in the early 17th century, though the community grew mainly in the 19th; by 1921 it numbered 336 residents (41%), rising to 456 by 1939. Most were murdered at Treblinka in late 1942. The cemetery's own existence is first documented in a 1711 Catholic parish visitation report, predating any record of its founding, and it was fenced by the Jewish community in 1926. Wartime and postwar destruction left it devastated - by the time Poland formally closed it in 1964, official documentation described the site as intended for tree planting, and only the foundations of a few broken tombstones survive today. Its boundaries remain faintly traceable via LIDAR, and a symbolic brick gateway echoing a menorah was erected at its edge in 1982.
